48F, EU OBSERVATION admission from EMERGENCY ROOM.
OUTCOME: discharged alive
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Other speech disturbance; Abdominal pain, epigastric; Nausea with vomiting; Fever, unspecified; Cough; Other respiratory abnormalities; Abdominal pain, right upper quadrant
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Other speech disturbance
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Hyposmolality and/or hyponatremia; Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease; End stage renal disease; Other chronic pain; Herpes simplex without mention of complication; Systemic lupus erythematosus; Chronic glomerulonephritis in diseases classified elsewhere; Anemia, unspecified; Thalassemia minor; Mitral valve disorders; Chronic diastolic heart failure; Congestive heart failure, unspecified
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Acquired absence of kidney
PROCEDURES: none
MEDICATIONS: Metoprolol Tartrate 100mg PO/NG; Docusate Sodium 100mg PO/NG; Labetalol 200mg PO/NG; sevelamer CARBONATE 2400mg PO; Acyclovir 200mg PO/NG; Lisinopril 80mg PO/NG; Influenza Vaccine Quadrivalent 0.5mL IM; Lidocaine 5% Patch 1PTCH TD; Acetaminophen 1000mg PO/NG; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 3mL IV; Omeprazole 20mg PO; Nephrocaps 1CAP PO/NG; Lorazepam 0.5mg PO/NG; Polyethylene Glycol 17g PO/NG
MICROBIOLOGY: none
SERVICES: MED
WARDS: Medicine; Emergency Department
_patient.note:
[1] The patient is a 48-year-old female admitted from the Emergency Room to EU Observation.
[2] The patient presented with other speech disturbance, abdominal pain, epigastric; nausea with vomiting, fever, unspecified; cough; other respiratory abnormalities; and abdominal pain, right upper quadrant.
[3] The primary diagnosis is other speech disturbance.
[4] The active diagnoses are hyposmolality and/or hyponatremia, hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease, end stage renal disease, other chronic pain, herpes simplex without mention of complication, systemic lupus erythematosus, chronic glomerulonephritis in diseases classified elsewhere, anemia, unspecified, thalassemia minor, mitral valve disorders, chronic diastolic heart failure, and congestive heart failure, unspecified.
[5] The patient has a past medical history of acquired absence of kidney.
[6] No procedures were performed.
[7] Medications administered include Metoprolol Tartrate 100mg PO/NG, Docusate Sodium 100mg PO/NG, Labetalol 200mg PO/NG, sevelamer CARBONATE 2400mg PO, Acyclovir 200mg PO/NG, Lisinopril 80mg PO/NG, Influenza Vaccine Quadrivalent 0.5mL IM, Lidocaine 5% Patch 1PTCH TD, Acetaminophen 1000mg PO/NG, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 3mL IV, Omeprazole 20mg PO, Nephrocaps 1CAP PO/NG, Lorazepam 0.5mg PO/NG, and Polyethylene Glycol 17g PO/NG.
[8] No microbiology results were obtained.
[9] The patient was managed by the MED service.
[10] The patient was admitted to the Medicine ward and the Emergency Department.
[11] The patient was discharged alive.
